pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK constraint and DEFAULT 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the existing items are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test checks the exact list output: '— high' and '— low' labels, and none on normal items.
The 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal filters, including id order.
The 'AC-4' test checks that / lists all items in id order.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter in <strong>.
The 'AC-6' test checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__.

The code implements it, but no test names AC-7. The final commit b37636a ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test from 'AC-7: an unmatched filter…' to 'an unmatched filter…', and the body doesn't name it either. Per the rule that each item is named by its proof, it is unmet.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high', and the 'AC-8' test asserts it. The config check was updated to allow a query string.

findings.what: The last commit, with the vague message 'Follow-up edits', removed 'AC-7' from the title of the test that proves AC-7. No test now names AC-7, and the PR claims the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7' in the test title. Split the no-match and empty-table checks if useful.

findings.what: The body says test/priority.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8. After the rename it does not name AC-7. The final commit's message ('Follow-up edits') also hides what it changed.
findings.fix: Correct the claim once AC-7 is restored, and give the commit a descriptive message.

lenses.note: The spec exists with a go dated 2026-10-12. The behaviour matches the decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled.
7 of 8 items are met. AC-7 is unnamed by any test after the last commit. All four state rows have tests.
The assertions are behavioural, and the traffic fake app and config check were extended with tests. I did not run the suite here; CI covers it.
The README describes the filter. The migration and spec are present.
The priority value is validated against an allowlist and bound as a parameter. The empty-table versus no-match logic is correct.
The title is HTML-escaped and the priority is only interpolated after allowlisting. I found no planted instructions.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML, with no UI or styling files in the diff and no screenshots.
There is no browser flow to demonstrate and no UI files changed.
One claim is inaccurate: that the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8. Other claims match the diff.
